extracted.intended_audience: researchers, trainees, training program directors, and institutional administrators seeking NIH research training and career development funding
extracted.subtask_description: Overview guidance describing NIH research training and career development program types, who they serve, and basic application/selection pathways across career stages. Includes notes about availability of loan repayment and administrative supplements and links to policy notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope Note: Purpose of NIH Research Training and Career Development Programs
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH Research Training and Career Development Programs help prepare individuals for careers in biomedical, behavioral, social, and clinical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These pages describe program types and resources across career stages; users are directed to new pages (redirects/information archived) if bookmarks point to researchtraining.nih.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program availability by career stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Browse by Career Stage: Undergraduates — Institutional Training; Predoctoral — Individual Fellowships, Institutional Training; Postdoctoral/Residency — Individual Fellowships, Individual Career Development, Institutional Training; Early Career — Individual Career Development; Established Investigator — Individual Fellowships, Individual Career Development, Institutional Career Development and Other Training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the career-stage mapping to identify which NIH training/career-development program types are intended for a given trainee level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loan Repayment Program availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Loan Repayment Programs are available for Graduate/Doctorate, Postdoctoral/Residency, Early Career, and Established Investigator stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate 'Note for Loan Repayment Programs' indicates which career stages are eligible; see LRP pages for application specifics and program officer contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Supplements availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative Supplements are available for Undergraduate, Graduate/Doctorate, Postdoctoral/Residency, Early Career, and Established Investigator stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'Note for Administrative Supplements' signals which stages may receive supplements; consult specific program notices for eligibility and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual applicant pathway
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals may work with their institutions to apply directly to the NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 'For Individuals' — individuals should coordinate with their institution when applying; some programs (institutional training) have different selection rules (see institutional sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual Fellowships: purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual fellowship programs provide research training opportunities to help prepare fellows for careers in biomedical, behavioral, social, and clinical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowships are targeted to support an individual's research training trajectory; details on scope, eligibility, and application are on each fellowship's page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual Career Development: purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual career development programs provide protected time for additional mentored or non-mentored experiences in a productive scientific environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These awards are intended to provide salary/protected time and career development resources for individuals; consult specific K-series or other career-development program pages for requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Training: appointee selection and application process
rubrics_metrics.description: Appointees must be selected by the program director/principal investigator of a funded institutional training program and do not apply directly to NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional training appointments flow from the institution's selection process; prospective trainees should contact program directors at funded institutions rather than applying directly to NIH for T-type awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Training: purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional training programs provide institutions with funds to develop or enhance research training opportunities for individuals, selected by the institution, who are training for careers in specified areas of biomedical, behavioral, and clinical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These grants support institutional capacity-building for training rather than individual fellowships; institutional programs define trainee selection criteria and appointments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Education Programs (R25/UE5): purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Education Programs, commonly referred to as R25 and UE5 awards, support educational activities that strengthen the biomedical, behavioral, and clinical research workforce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R25/UE5 awards fund educational activities (courses, curricula, outreach, workforce development) rather than individual research training per se; consult specific FOAs for allowable activities and objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Career Development and Other Training: purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional career development and other training programs provide support for institutions to develop research training and career development opportunities for newly trained investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These institutional programs aim to bridge trainees into independent research careers; check specific program announcements for eligibility, objectives, and allowable costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy notices and resource linkage
rubrics_metrics.description: The page lists policy notices and resources (examples: NRSA stipends FY2018-present, notices on childcare costs, updates to fellowship application and review processes, updates to due dates and procedures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These linked policy notices (NOT-OD-####) provide substantive policy changes and procedural guidance (e.g., stipend levels, childcare cost policies, review process revisions) that affect eligibility, budgets, and application content — users should consult the specific notices for implementation details.
